events.markdown: I’ll check our bindings and look at how other harnesses get terminal-style output. You’re right that this should ideally be presentation behavior, not something the agent has to remember to request on every command.

I’m using OpenAI Docs for the Codex execution constraints, and implementation code for the other harnesses. The important distinction is who controls execution: a client that owns the shell process can preserve terminal output for you while sending cleaned-up text to the model. Harness currently receives commands executed by Codex, so I’ll check how much control that path exposes.

events.markdown: Zed has a concrete version of what you’re describing: its agent tool embeds a real terminal view for the user, then extracts plain text from the terminal buffer for the model. That’s more than styling a plain-text output box.
